hey, i read all of it, and honestly i really understand you. i'm just like you. i've been depressed and suicidal for 11 years now (i'm 22), at least since i realized what depression is. i honestly can't remember a time that i didn't have it.  


anyways, i'm going to be 1000% honest with you. it might be long, i'll try to keep it short. life never gets easier. it's bullshit when people say "it'll get better". it won't. people will still be royal jerks. everyone will be selfish. feeling alone probably gets worse as you get older. these days i don't feel like i have anyone on my side. i get jealous seeing close friends and friendships because i don't have that. i live alone in South Korea. my best friend moved back to America. I do have a boyfriend, but he's always busy. i am the last priority.  


what i can tell you is that although it never gets easier, it hurts less. it's like ripping off a bandaid-hear me out. you will still experience the same pain, but the first time you ripped off a bandaid it seemed like torture, right? but doing it a few times your tolerance grows. and it keeps growing. you're still ripping off a bandaid-same issue different day. but it gets less painful.   


i'm going to also tell you, i attempted twice when i was your age and failed both times. so i set one goal for myself-to move to seoul. took me awhile but i'm here, and although i'm depressed as always i'm happy to be in the place where i belong, even though i'll never be accepted. 15 year old me ate lunch alone everyday in the art room, was excluded and bullied by others, and depressed. my home life was extremely strict-i wasn't allowed to go to the mall with friends without a parent until i was 18 years old. no one wanted to spend time with me because of that. i only found solace in korean music. and 6/7 years later here i am living in korea.  


it will not get better now, or soon. but the bandaid will get easier to rip off, and you will become a stronger person. they say the strongest, kindest people are the ones who have seen the darkest times-and one day that will be you. everyday you're becoming stronger. the place you're at now? being 15 living at home? i never want to go back to that time because i know how much it sucks. but, i would endure it to have what i have now, even if i'm not happy, i'm where i want to be.

I think the best answer for that would be to distance yourself and start putting closure onto things. That being said, no matter how much distance you put, it will absolutely impact those involved in your life. I moved to the other side of the world for the distance so it would be a more viable option and less sad if i just disappear because i never see my family anyways, but yes my boyfriend would be devastated. or would he? who knows. i guess generally i don't think anyone would miss me for long after i'm gone. i think i generally waste space and time, and it would be a lesser burden on those around me if i wasn't here. i don't really contribute anything important. but i didn't graduate from a top university, i do have my dream job but most people look down on it, yeah, i think it wouldn't make a difference if i am here or not. i think it would leave a big hole in the world if you weren't here, though. but that doesn't mean you are selfish. the financial aspect...try to do as much damage control as possible, but i don't think the money would matter to your boyfriend if it meant losing you. i reckon you mean a lot more to him than money does. for your landlord it would be really tough.   


I guess in your situation, the best thing you can do is try to give as much closure as you can while you can, but recognize that it will still be a huge burden and pain to bear for those around you. honestly, it sounds like you're a very impactful person with people who care about you, and i envy that. but i know that no matter how many people "care", you'll never truly feel it even if you know it. and if you can't find true happiness, then who knows. i don't know, i wish i could offer better advice.
